proposition: According to Melvin-Koushki, Nasr calls Ibn Turka a peripatetic-illuminationist philosopher and Sufi of the Ibn ʿArabi school linking Tusi and Sadra, and Ziai a Shiʿi thinker harmonizing religion and philosophy to promote the political authority of the ʿulamaʾ; MK calls Ziai's statement incorrect and anachronistic.

mediation.note: The position is this scholar's own; we have it only as summarised by Melvin-Koushki.
MK argues a rival reading (Ibn Turka as occult philosopher) and in places calls this reading an error; his summary may compress or foreshorten it.
